script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: WHO I AM

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

MRS. JONES, 40s, is making breakfast while her children, JACK, 12, and SALLY, 10, sit at the table.

MRS. JONES
(to herself)
Why do they insist on asking me who I am?

JACK
(looking up from his cereal)
Mom, you're a mom.

SALLY
(rolling her eyes)
And a wife.

MRS. JONES
(sighs)
Yes, I am. But there's more to me than just that.

JACK
(puzzled)
What do you mean?

MRS. JONES
(smiling)
One day, you'll understand.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Jones sits on the couch, scrolling through old family photos on her laptop. She comes across a picture of herself from college. She looks different - younger, carefree, with wild hair and a big smile.

MRS. JONES
(to herself)
Who was that girl?

INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Jones' husband, MR. JONES, 45, enters the room. He sits on the bed next to her, looking at the laptop screen.

MR. JONES
You look beautiful.

MRS. JONES
(smiling)
Thank you. But it's not just about looks. It's about who I was before I became a mom and a wife.

MR. JONES
(nods)
I understand. But you're still the same person, just with different responsibilities.

MRS. JONES
(sighs)
Maybe. But I want them to know there's more to me than just being their mom.

EXT. PARK - DAY

Mrs. Jones sits on a bench, watching Jack and Sally play on the swings. She looks pensive, deep in thought.

Suddenly, a woman, MS. RICHMOND, 50s, approaches and sits down next to her.

MS. RICHMOND
(smiling)
Hi. I see you're a mother.

MRS. JONES
(looking up)
Yes. And sometimes I feel like I've lost myself in motherhood.

MS. RICHMOND
(nods)
I know the feeling. But it's never too late to rediscover who you are.

INT. ART GALLERY - DAY

Mrs. Jones stands in front of a painting, her eyes filled with emotion. She turns to see Jack and Sally standing behind her, looking at the same painting.

JACK
(pointing to the painting)
This is you, Mom.

SALLY
(nods)
You're an artist.

MRS. JONES
(tears in her eyes)
I hadn't thought of that in years.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Jones sits at the piano, playing a melody she used to play before she became a mom. The kids come in, listening quietly.

JACK
(amazed)
Mom, you're amazing!

SALLY
(nods)
I had no idea.

MR. JONES
(proudly)
I always did.

MRS. JONES
(smiling)
Thank you. I'm more than just a mom and a wife. I'm an artist.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
